comparator.name: Computational Social Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The regulations require five 30 EC modules and allow 30 EC of electives. Each required module builds on earlier work. The final capstone combines social research and data science to develop and implement a digital intervention with an external partner.
components: Foundation: Appreciating the complexity of social challenges
Building blocks: Experimenting with digital interventions for behavioural change
Connections: Linking data for better interventions in health or mobility systems
Structures: Applying responsible AI to reduce inequality
Electives, minor, internship or study abroad
Capstone: Making social change with digital innovations

core: Computational social science combining human behaviour, social research and data-driven public problem solving
Programming, data analysis, visualisation and machine learning for social impact
Project-based digital intervention, stakeholder collaboration and responsible innovation
adjacent: Climate, mobility and data-driven environmental intervention
Responsible AI, inequality, surveillance and algorithmic power
questions: How can computational methods turn social evidence into responsible digital solutions?
How can data and digital interventions improve climate, mobility or health systems?
How do surveillance, algorithms and AI reproduce or reduce social inequality?

candidates.label: Climate, spatial data and environmental policy
Responsible AI, inequality and digital society
Health systems and digital public services
candidates.reason: The Connections module supports a health systems option with its own application focus. The three selected options already reach the limit. The closest option includes behavioural and organisational research.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: Develops academic writing, source evaluation, reflection and collaborative work for later projects.
Uses regression, instrumental variables and simulation to distinguish causal questions from prediction in an empirical paper.
Builds a strategy for responsible digital change using industry cases and analysis of stakeholder value and organisational effects.
Uses design thinking, customer validation and team prototyping to develop and test a venture idea.
Uses surveys, sampling, study design and inferential statistics to collect and analyse evidence about people.
Examines motivation, group dynamics and workplace culture through cases, simulations and research synthesis, informing organisational change.
Examines bias, surveillance, interpretability and accountability using ethical frameworks and cases.
Uses SQL, relational design and authorisation to organise and govern access to structured data.
Implements and evaluates search and graph algorithms that support analysis of linked data and networks.
Cleans, combines and visualises data in R, including spatial and text data.
Fits and validates predictive and exploratory models and compares their performance on real datasets.
Trains and evaluates neural networks for tabular, image and text prediction, building technical depth for examining algorithmic decisions.
Develops Python programming, data structures, testing and debugging for computational problem-solving.
Develops linear algebra and calculus for modelling, optimisation and later machine learning.
Uses matrix decompositions, least squares and principal components to represent and analyse multidimensional data.
Examines and tests nature-based infrastructure for flood protection, coastal planning and ecosystem connectivity.
Uses Zeeland projects to assess water infrastructure, flood adaptation and the governance of delta systems.
Uses stakeholder interviews, policy-option matrices and evaluation to analyse decisions about sustainability.
Compares environmental hazards and evaluates measures that reduce risks from droughts and other hazards.
Uses GIS, satellites and drone data to integrate, analyse and visualise spatial evidence about environmental change.
Uses earth-system models, proxies and tracers to investigate climate and greenhouse gas pathways.
Develops physical and mathematical foundations for understanding climate processes and interpreting evidence about sustainability.
Builds scientific measurement and evidence appraisal for environmental case work and prepares for spatial planning and energy design.
Connects climate drivers and impacts to adaptation, mitigation, governance and justice.
Evaluates energy-use patterns and transition options through a technical and economic study for a partner company.
Uses literature review and research design to investigate a regional sustainability question supplied by an external organisation.
Applies GIS and remote sensing to spatial planning problems in disaster response and environmental monitoring.
Uses socio-legal research and case law to study how law shapes justice, social control and social change.
Uses rights frameworks, treaties and cases to examine dignity, equality and freedom of expression in evaluating digital policy.
Uses comparative cases and democracy data to examine institutions, participation and the context of public interventions.
Analyses policy development across jurisdictions and communicates findings through policy memos.
Applies sociological theories and research questions to class, gender, race and social networks.
Uses interviews, focus groups, observation and thematic coding to analyse stakeholder perspectives.
Uses social theory and cases to examine power, intersectionality and the production of inequality.
Compares environmental justice movements and forms of collective action as a concrete domain for examining unequal impacts and responses.
Uses social theory and empirical group research to study civil society, digital publics and collective action.
Introduces learning, social influence and behavioural research and prepares students for advanced evidence synthesis.
Examines social influence, persuasion and prejudice through empirical social psychology and research design.
Develops experimental design, statistical modelling and effect-size interpretation for testing behavioural claims.
Uses systematic reviews, bias appraisal and meta-analysis to combine evidence across studies and judge intervention effects.
Uses audience analysis, argument and persuasive writing to communicate the rationale for public action.
Applies ethical persuasion to sustainability messaging with climate researchers and tests communication ideas through action research.
Analyses how media forms and technologies shape identity, representation and power.
Uses research on race, media and narrative power to examine how communication can reproduce or contest unequal representation.

alternatives.label: Computational social science and public innovation
alternatives.labelReason: Python, sociology and research design support later work in modelling and experimentation. Policy, persuasion and organisational strategy bring the methods to public and organisational problems.
alternatives.concept: Combines Python, data analysis and machine learning with social research and behavioural science. Courses in policy, entrepreneurship and communication explore how evidence can inform public interventions.
progression: Python, sociology and research design support later work in modelling and experimentation. Policy, persuasion and organisational strategy bring the methods to public and organisational problems.

alternatives.label: Climate, spatial data and environmental policy
alternatives.labelReason: Climate science, programming and quantitative foundations support later work in spatial analysis, machine learning, governance and energy design. The introductory project supplies an early experience of an applied sustainability question.
alternatives.concept: Uses climate science, GIS and social research to study environmental risks and how communities respond. Spatial planning, delta governance and energy design apply these skills to environmental decisions.
progression: Climate science, programming and quantitative foundations support later work in spatial analysis, machine learning, governance and energy design. The introductory project supplies an early experience of an applied sustainability question.
alternatives.distinctness: Climate science, GIS, spatial planning and delta adaptation drive the selection.

alternatives.label: Responsible AI, inequality and digital society
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, maths, research design and social theory precede deeper work in machine learning, civil society and media. AI ethics and rights frameworks support evaluation of the social effects of algorithmic decisions.
alternatives.concept: Combines machine learning and data management with sociology, law and AI ethics to study the effects of algorithms on inequality. Media analysis examines how representation and power shape digital life.
progression: Programming, maths, research design and social theory precede deeper work in machine learning, civil society and media. AI ethics and rights frameworks support evaluation of the social effects of algorithmic decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Neural networks, data management, law, critical sociology and media representation drive the selection.

blocks: Both teach data preparation and visualisation. UCR uses R in a dedicated data science course, while UvA combines these skills with Python and social research projects.
Both build and evaluate predictive models. UvA combines modelling with stakeholder engagement and analysis of algorithmic bias.
Both analyse stakeholders and develop policy responses to complex systems. UCR focuses on sustainability governance. UvA develops an intervention plan for a health or mobility system.
Both involve team research on a problem from an external partner. UCR investigates a regional sustainability question. UvA also implements a digital intervention in its final semester.
Both use design thinking and prototyping. UCR tests a venture idea, while UvA tests a digital intervention for behaviour change.
The fifth semester offers 30 EC of elective study, a minor, an approved internship or study abroad.

selection.assessment: The broad option brings computation, behavioural research and public problem solving together. The climate option emphasises spatial data and environmental policy. The responsible AI option emphasises models, inequality and digital power. The three distinct options reach the maximum.

notes.text: UvA teaches social research, computation and intervention design together in semester-long projects. UCR develops related skills across separate courses. The required UvA capstone includes implementing a digital intervention for an external partner.
UvA reserves the fifth semester for 30 EC of electives, a minor, an approved internship or study abroad.

audience.programmeDescription: Computational Social Science at the University of Amsterdam combines social research and computing to investigate public problems and develop digital interventions. Students work on projects about climate, surveillance, health or mobility, and inequality.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines social research, computing and public problem solving. The other options concentrate on spatial data and environmental policy, or on responsible AI and inequality.

componentNotes.y1-building: Students design and pilot a digital intervention for behaviour change.
componentNotes.y2-connections: Students prepare a plan for an intervention in a health or mobility system.
componentNotes.y2-structures: Students build a predictive model and examine risks of algorithmic bias.
componentNotes.y3-capstone: Teams submit a research report and implement a digital intervention with an external partner.
